data.description:
# Card outlines and card positions move when a card is added to the hand

## Problem Statement

When a `HandView` is configured with a known capacity (`maxSlots`) and ghost
position outlines (`showPositionOutlines: true`), both the card row **and** the
outline row are laid out relative to the *current* card count. Adding a card
therefore re-centres the whole row: every existing card and every slot shifts
laterally, and it only stops moving once the hand reaches `maxSlots`. The user
observes "the left card becomes centred and the two to the right are pushed
right; then when another card is added they all move left one slot".

Slot positions should be derived from the hand's **capacity**, not its current
size, so an occupied slot stays put as cards are added and the row only
re-lays when a slot is added (capacity change).

## Users

- **Player (Main Street, Gym)** — builds a stable spatial memory of where each
  held card sits; cards appear in the next free slot instead of shuffling under
  the pointer. Also keeps the ghost capacity outline in the same place as the
  card that later fills it.
- **Developer** — relies on `HandView` for layout; no scene-level workaround or
  bespoke hand rendering should be required to get stable slots.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, when I buy a second business card into my (capacity
  3) hand, the first card stays exactly where it was and the new card appears to
  its right.
- As a Gym user, drawing a 6th card into the 7-slot hand does not move the
  first five cards.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With `maxSlots` set, the set of outline slot positions for a given capacity
   is **identical** for a hand of 0, 1, … `maxSlots` cards (measured: the
   `outlineRects[i].x` for every `i` is unchanged across `setCards` of each
   size).
2. Adding a card places it in the next empty slot to the right of the occupied
   run, and every already-placed card keeps its pre-add position (measured:
   for `addCard`, `sprite[i].x` before === after for all pre-existing `i`).
3. Occupied outline slots still sit at the exact card position and rotation
   (`rect.x/y/rotation === sprite.x/y/rotation`), and extra capacity slots still
   render below every card — the CG-0MT6ER7YY003G680 invariant is preserved.
4. Changing capacity (`setMaxSlots(n)`) re-lays the whole row and always yields
   exactly `n` slots; this is the only mutation that may move existing cards.
5. The empty-hand capacity row is unchanged from today's behaviour — `maxSlots`
   straight/arc slots centred on the hand centre — so an empty hand still shows
   the full capacity in the same place the cards will occupy.
6. Unit tests (`tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`) verify AC 1–5, including a
   regression test that asserts positions do **not** move across successive
   `addCard`/`setCards` calls up to capacity, and that `setMaxSlots` does
   re-layout.
7. Browser tests (`tests/handView/gym-handpile-outlines.browser.test.ts`,
   `tests/main-street/hand-outlines.browser.test.ts`) assert slot/card position
   stability across a draw/add, not just alignment at a single hand size.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (Hand capacity outlines), `AGENTS.md` if the
   documented behaviour changes, and any relevant Gym/docs entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the shared `HandView` (`src/ui/HandView.ts`), not as a
  scene-specific workaround, because both Main Street and the Gym use
  `maxSlots` + outlines.
- Preserve the existing empty-hand capacity row (centred on `centerX`): that
  row *is* the fixed slot template, so no visual change is expected for an
  empty hand.
- The fix must honour the existing layout options: `spacing`, `maxWidth`
  compression, `arcRadius`, `maxRotationDegrees`, `cardWidth`/`cardHeight`,
  `centerX`, and both `horizontal` and `vertical` `layoutDirection`.
- Cards fill the capacity slots left-to-right; the row is not re-anchored per
  card count.
- The layout must remain deterministic (same inputs → same positions).
- Vertical cascade already derives positions from `baseY + i * spacing`, so it
  is already card-count independent; the change must not regress it.
- Over-capacity hands (transiently `cards.length > maxSlots`) are best-effort:
  the first `maxSlots` slots stay fixed, outlines stay capped at `maxSlots`,
  and overflow cards continue to the right with the same step. Normal gameplay
  prevents this state.

## Existing State

- `src/ui/HandView.ts`:
  - `computeCardPositions()` (≈ line 1719) computes the card row with
    `layoutCardPositions({ count: this.cards.length, … })` → the row is
    centred on the **current** card count, so it moves as cards are added.
  - `_computeOutlineSlots()` (≈ line 1299) handles two branches: with no cards
    it lays out the full `maxSlots` row (the desired fixed template); with cards
    it ghosts `computeCardPositions()` and appends extras to the right of the
    last card, so the occupied slots inherit the moving card layout.
  - `_outlineCount()` returns `maxSlots` when defined, else `cards.length`.
  - `_updateOutlinePositions()` / `applyLayout()` reposition and rebuild
    outlines on every mutation.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` — already provides the centred, optionally
  compressed row maths needed to build a capacity template; no change expected.
- Main Street wires `showPositionOutlines: true`, `maxSlots:
  state.maxHandSize`, `centerX: handCenterX`, and syncs capacity with
  `setMaxSlots()` (`MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`, `MainStreetRendererLayout.ts`).
- Gym wires `showPositionOutlines: true`, `maxSlots: 7` in
  `GymHandPileScene.ts`.
- Existing tests assert alignment at a *single* hand size but never stability
  across adds: `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`,
  `tests/handView/gym-handpile-outlines.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/hand-outlines.browser.test.ts`.

## Desired Change

- Compute the slot template once from capacity: when `maxSlots` is defined,
  derive the `maxSlots` row positions (using the same `layoutCardPositions` /
  arc maths used today for the empty-hand outline row) and place the first
  `this.cards.length` cards into it.
- Reuse that same template in `_computeOutlineSlots()` so occupied slots ghost
  their card positions and extra slots continue the template to the right —
  producing one consistent capacity row for both cards and outlines at every
  hand size.
- Keep `showPositionOutlines` purely visual: capacity-driven layout is keyed on
  `maxSlots !== undefined`, so toggling outlines off does not move cards.
- Leave hands that do not declare `maxSlots` on the existing centred-on-count
  layout.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `computeCardPositions()`, `_computeOutlineSlots()`: derive card/outline positions from the `maxSlots` capacity template instead of `cards.length`.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` — Likely unchanged; reused to build the capacity row.
- `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts` — Add stability/regression tests (AC 1–5).
- `tests/handView/gym-handpile-outlines.browser.test.ts` — Assert slot/card stability across a draw.
- `tests/main-street/hand-outlines.browser.test.ts` — Assert stability across an added card; re-check click/drag/transfer paths that assume the hand centre.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Update "Hand capacity outlines" to document capacity-driven (stable) slot semantics.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` — Help text only if the documented behaviour wording changes.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` / `MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` — Verify no scene-level assumption about per-count centring; likely no code change.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MT6ER7YY003G680** — "Show an outline of card positions in the hand"
  (completed): introduced `showPositionOutlines` / `maxSlots` and the layout
  code this bug corrects.
- **CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD** — "Main Street: merge business hand + held event into
  one horizontal 3-card hand" (completed): established the 3-card hand and
  `handCenterX` anchoring.
- **CG-0MQSFGE540037N6S** / **CG-0MQRXO41D009DH26** — "Write Tests for Staff
  Cards & Hand Capacity" / "Implement Staff Cards & Hand Capacity System"
  (completed): runtime capacity changes that exercise `setMaxSlots`.
- **CG-0MS937FT9006273E** — "Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight renders over
  cards to the right" (completed): the depth-ordering pattern the outline
  depths build on.
- Automated `find-related` report (below) surfaced: CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7,
  CG-0MQ54PYAJ001XCUG, CG-0MLTFFGBH1CEPC7J (low signal for this layout bug).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption (design):** The fixed slot row is the *same* centred capacity
  row currently rendered for an empty hand. Consequently a 1-card hand places
  that card in the **leftmost** capacity slot (left of the hand centre) rather
  than at the centre. This is the direct reading of "the position of the cards
  should not move unless a new slot is added", and it keeps the empty-hand
  appearance unchanged.
- **Assumption (scope):** Capacity-driven layout keys off `maxSlots !==
  undefined`, independent of whether outlines are currently visible, so
  toggling outlines never moves cards.
- **Assumption (right):** Cards fill capacity slots left-to-right; the row is
  never right- or centre-anchored per card count.
- **Risk:** Main Street's `handCenterX` anchoring and the hand→street transfer
  animation (`hiddenTransferSourceCardIds`) may assume a centred row for hit
  testing or source coordinates. Mitigation: run the Main Street browser suite
  and the drag/click/transfer flows; adjust only if a real regression appears.
- **Risk:** `maxWidth` compression means the step depends on `maxSlots`, so a
  capacity change can shift positions more than one slot. Acceptable — capacity
  change is an explicitly allowed re-layout.
- **Risk:** Over-capacity transient states. Mitigation: define best-effort
  behaviour above and unit-test it.
- **Scope creep guard:** Games without `maxSlots`, and any non-outline hand
  behaviour, must remain on the existing centred-on-count layout. A broader
  "slots everywhere" redesign (e.g. right-to-left hands, per-slot assignment)
  is out of scope and should be raised as a new work item if desired.

## Clarifying Questions & Answers (Appendix)

The seed context plus repository inspection answered the material design
questions; no operator/producer questions were required before drafting. The
resolutions are **agent assumptions** derived from the requirement (not
producer statements); each is labelled for confirmation during review:

- Q: Which layout should a capacity hand use? — **Assumption (agent):** the
  fixed centred capacity row already rendered for an empty hand, with cards
  filling it left-to-right. Evidence: `_computeOutlineSlots()` empty-hand
  branch already produces this row; the bug report only objects to the
  movement, implying the empty-hand row is acceptable. The only alternative
  (anchor slot 0 at the hand centre) would make the empty-hand outlines jump
  when the first card is drawn, so it does not satisfy "positions should not
  move".
- Q: Does the fix apply to the shared `HandView` or Main Street only? —
  **Assumption (agent):** shared `HandView`, keyed on `maxSlots`. Evidence:
  both `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` and `GymHandPileScene.ts` enable
  `maxSlots` + outlines and exhibit the same defect.
- Q: Should toggling outlines on/off move cards? — **Assumption (agent):** no;
  layout is keyed on capacity (`maxSlots`), not on `showPositionOutlines`.
- Q: What happens when a slot is added? — **Assumption (agent):** the row
  re-lays out (existing `setMaxSlots()` behaviour), which is the one case where
  movement is expected.
- **Producer confirmation requested (non-blocking):** the consequence of this
  design is that a 1-card hand shows its card in the **leftmost** capacity slot
  (off-centre) rather than centred. This is the only user-visible outcome that
  changes for existing scenes; it is logically required by "positions should
  not move unless a new slot is added".
